newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Boehler Q1 net down, order intake up.
newsitem.headline: Boehler Q1 net down, order intake up.

text.p: Austrian high-grade steel maker Boehler-Uddeholm said on Thursday net profit fell in the first quarter while order intake increased four percent.
In a statement, Boehler said net profit before minority interests was 117 million schillings after 315 million in the first three months of 1996.
"This was due to the record year 1995 in which lead times were extended, resulting in many deliveries actually being made in the first five months of 1996," the firm said.
The positive trend in incoming orders continued in April, when order intake was up 37 percent over April 1996. Orders for special steel long products rose 42 percent.

First quarter turnover fell to 4.17 billion schillings from 4.97 billion, Boehler said. Earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) were 220 million schillings after 510 million and pre-tax profit fell to 166 million schillings from 443 million.
The firm noted improved demand in Germany and Scandinavia and forecast a slight pick-up in overall volume in the second half of 1997. -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
